title: Production Readiness
outcome: The complete NoorPath MVP is demonstrably safe, recoverable, observable and operable for a controlled production release, with exact evidence for critical journeys, security, data integrity, accessibility, performance, deployment and rollback.
actor: NoorPath Product Owner, release operator, engineering team and authorized operational staff responsible for approving, releasing and supporting the MVP.
modules: Each domain module remains responsible for its own invariants, migrations, recovery behavior, telemetry and operational commands.
Platform and Delivery own environment configuration, deployment, rollback, health checks and release evidence without bypassing module boundaries.
Security and Accounts own authentication, authorization, secret handling, privileged access and privacy verification.
Operations composes customer and operator exceptions through approved commands and documented runbooks rather than direct database mutation.
Web and API hosts provide truthful health, error, accessibility and performance behavior for the certified release candidate.
Product Owner owns release-scope acceptance and the explicit production deployment decision for the exact certified commit.
routes: Public discovery -> Package details -> Quote -> Inventory hold -> Booking -> Payment -> Confirmation
Authenticated customer -> My Journey -> Documents -> Visa -> Family and Mahram -> Cancellation and refund status
Authorized operator -> Package authoring -> Pricing and inventory -> Review and publish
Authorized operator -> Package management -> Booking management -> Document review -> Visa processing -> Operational support -> Cancellation and refund recovery
Platform Administrator -> Administration -> Publication approvals -> Final independent publication review
Release operator -> Preflight -> Migration -> Deployment -> Health verification -> Smoke tests -> Release decision
Release operator -> Failed release -> Rollback -> Data and health verification -> Incident evidence
acceptance: The exact release-scope slice set and release candidate SHA are recorded and unchanged throughout certification.
Critical customer and operator journeys pass end-to-end against the production-like environment using safe test data.

Every release-scope page, section, menu, breadcrumb, card, redirect and API-generated action target is reachable through its intended clickable navigation on desktop and mobile, or is explicitly recorded as BLOCKED_IDENTITY with the required identity/configuration and follow-up verification step.
Direct-route tests supplement but do not replace click-through verification from the real public, customer, operator, administration and operational source controls.
Authentication, authorization, account isolation, operator isolation and privileged-action controls are reverified across all release-scope surfaces.
Secret scanning, configuration review and log inspection show no exposed credentials, tokens, payment payloads, traveller data or document data.
Every registered migration applies from an empty database and from the approved prior production baseline without pending model drift.
Backup creation, restore and post-restore integrity checks are demonstrated with recorded timestamps, ownership and recovery results.
Deployment and rollback are executed through the approved manual workflow using the exact certified SHA and leave the system in a known state.
Liveness and readiness endpoints truthfully distinguish process health from dependency readiness and are verified during normal, degraded and recovery conditions.
Monitoring, logs, traces and alerts provide sufficient evidence to diagnose failed payment, confirmation, document, visa, cancellation, refund and migration outcomes.
Baseline load and latency checks meet Product Owner-approved thresholds for the pilot traffic profile without overselling inventory or duplicating financial effects.
Accessibility, keyboard operation, focus, target size, text scaling, reflow, reduced motion and serious/critical automated checks pass on critical screens.
Visual regression confirms all release-scope customer and operator surfaces remain consistent with the approved NoorPath visual baseline.
Operational runbooks identify owner, trigger, diagnosis, safe action, escalation and recovery verification for every critical failure mode.
Known risks, accepted limitations, environment-specific exclusions and go/no-go criteria are explicit and approved.
The Product Owner approves the exact certified release candidate SHA before merge.
Production deployment remains a separate explicit approval after merge and is never implied by certification.
policyDecisionsRequired: The release-scope slice list and any explicitly deferred MVP capability.
The pilot traffic, latency, error-rate and concurrency thresholds used for performance acceptance.
Recovery-point and recovery-time expectations for the pilot, including backup retention and restore ownership.
The minimum monitoring and alerting set, notification recipients and escalation path.
The production change window, release operator, rollback authority and go/no-go participants.
The acceptable known-risk register and which risks block release.
Whether production refund execution, document storage, external providers or other fail-closed integrations remain disabled at launch.
The exact post-deployment smoke-test set and observation period required before declaring the release stable.
exclusions: New customer or operator features unrelated to release readiness.
Architecture rewrites, service decomposition, Kubernetes, multi-region deployment or speculative scaling work.
Unapproved production enablement of refunds, storage, notifications or external-provider integrations.
Destructive production testing or the use of real customer, passport, payment or visa data in certification.
Direct database correction as a substitute for module-owned recovery commands.
Automatic production deployment when the planning or runtime PR is merged.
Long-term enterprise SRE maturity beyond the minimum pilot release and support boundary.
